summary: The code core stands: the morph.css deletion (+7/−29, 329 lines) is exactly the re-anchored target (ledger :271 — line drifted from every report's citation; substance identical in all three), the backdrop-root diagnosis is correct (.dock-plate is a direct child of .glass-dock and carries the dock partial's one backdrop-filter, dock.css:73; any filter on the root, blur(0px) included, flattens the lens), delete-not-retarget is sound (no safe host exists), clean break honored, both known CSS traps avoided, all targeted suites green (re-run this seat). The approach does not fall. But the roster clause "born-RED on PagerDots.vue:493" (TERMINAL-ROSTER:157, ledger :271) is unmet on its face: the delivered gate is GREEN at HEAD, pins the census exact-equality, and positively asserts the defect precondition — it goes RED when #40 W-PAGER cures the stack and when #55 WATERCOLOR-RELOCATE kills the ornament, punishing both cures it exists to demand, against the repo's own it.fails born-RED idiom (token-hygiene.test.ts:131). Verified secondary defects: the census-exclusion comment credits a provably inert lookbehind (HandMark is excluded by attribute `=` syntax, not the `:` class); the mechanized fence misses @media-nested decls, non-root-subject ancestors of lenses (.dock-layers), attr-bracket selectors, and out-of-dir .glass-dock rules (glass-capsule.css:167,170 prove they exist) while spending ~110 lines of bespoke parser where a ~12-line whole-tree allowlist (one live filter decl remains: icon-button.css:92) is simpler and stronger; the fence comment mints a "never a filter" bloom ruling on #47/#48 turf that contradicts #48's banked "sibling blur-resolve" (TERMINAL-ROSTER:198) and re-attaches the dock fence to a gate the roster re-scoped to drop "dock"; impl's F2 mischaracterizes same-element filter+backdrop-filter as the ancestor backdrop-root class; the adaptive-legibility.css:132-145 dead --dock-reveal-blur carve now sits under a lying comment (zero readers, confirmed); and no row-7 execution record exists for #47 to cite (every landed peer banked one; ledger row still reads UNSTARTED). Keep the source edit verbatim; the cures are the test rewrite, a 4-line comment reword, and two orchestrator-side items that fit the ⊕²⁰(e) consolidated dock cure round already held behind this verdict.

cures.title: C1 — re-latch the unit case born-RED (roster clause; the headline)
cures.detail: Rewrite tests/styles/stacked-url-filter.test.ts it() #2: assert ZERO files paint filter: url(#…) inside a backdrop-filtered subtree, latched born-RED via the house it.fails idiom (token-hygiene.test.ts:131 precedent), failure message naming PagerDots.vue:493 and #40 W-PAGER as the owner of the flip. Drop the exact-equality census pin (:111-114) and the .glass-pager-ring defect-precondition assert (:120-124) — both are fail-on-fix against #40 and #55 WATERCOLOR-RELOCATE. Mechanize 'stacked' (backdrop-filter ancestry) rather than pinning it by one hardcoded regex against one file; delete or correct the inert-lookbehind rationale at :23-25 (HandMark is excluded by attribute `=` syntax, and it genuinely paints filter:url(#…) as an SVG presentation attribute — the exclusion decision must be stated on its real grounds or dropped).

cures.title: C2 — collapse the dock fence to the whole-tree allowlist form
cures.detail: Replace it() #1's ~110-line selector parser with: zero filter declarations under src/components/dock/**/*.css outside a one-entry named allowlist (controls/icon-button.css:92, routed to #47). ~12 lines, no postcss selector resolution, and it closes all four verified holes: @media-nested decls (the rule?.type !== 'rule' early-return), non-root subjects that are still ancestors of capsule lenses (.dock-layers — named by the fence comment itself), attr selectors with spaces (split() breaks), and .glass-dock rules authored outside dock/ can be caught by one extra whole-src grep for filter decls under a .glass-dock-subject if desired. Un-bundle the header: the dock fence is the #7→#47 design fence, NOT an arm of G-NO-STACKED-URL-FILTER — the roster re-scope drops 'dock' from the gate (TERMINAL-ROSTER:157, :198).

cures.title: C3 — reword the morph.css fence comment (4 lines, keep the deletion verbatim)
cures.detail: At morph.css:66-72: (a) state the law as ancestor-of-lens — a filter on .glass-dock or any ancestor of a backdrop-filtered box (.dock-plate; the active .glass-capsule controls) flattens that lens — resolving the ':68 one backdrop-filter' vs ':71 capsule lenses' internal tension; (b) strike 'GF-DOCK expresses bloom in geometry/opacity/crossfade (#48's own score), never a filter' — it mints on #47/#48 turf and contradicts #48's banked 'sibling blur-resolve' (TERMINAL-ROSTER:198) and #47's restored-bloom clause (E2); the fence forbids the mechanism over the lens, the expression is #47/#48's; (c) attribute the fence to #47 (GF-DOCK); (d) one honest clause that the fence covers authored CSS only — the JS inline blur channel (useElementMorph.ts:229; useLiquidReveal.ts:74 and useDockCtaReceive.ts:245 default blur??4) is live, structurally invisible to this case, and owned by the motion rows.

cures.title: C4 — orchestrator-side: the adaptive-legibility residue (wall-widening, fits ⊕²⁰(e))
cures.detail: Delete the dead --dock-reveal-blur: 0px PRM carve at src/components/dock/styles/adaptive-legibility.css:132-145 (zero readers, confirmed by grep — the sole hit is the definition) and its now-false comment ('The self-blur is now gated to [data-morphing]' describes a deleted mechanism); fix the index.css clause citing 'the PRM reveal-blur carve' as the partial's split-out reason. 13 lines, zero behavior change, one file outside the seat's wall — lands cleanly in the consolidated dock/drawer cure round ⊕²⁰(e) already holds behind this verdict.

cures.title: C5 — orchestrator-side: bank the row-7 record and correct F2's routing
cures.detail: Bank docs/tranches/BK/execution/2026-08-03-row7-*/ (every landed peer row has one; ledger :271 still reads UNSTARTED) so #47's 'after #6/#26/#7-fence' clause has a citable artifact that survives GF-DOCK's rewrite of morph.css — the fence currently lives only in a comment inside the file #47 rewrites plus a test keyed to a class name #47/#72 may rename. In the record, route icon-button.css:92 to #47 as a SUSPICION stated correctly: filter+backdrop-filter on the SAME element (DockControl.vue:93) is not the ancestor backdrop-root class (both challengers right, impl's F2 wrong); the real issue is the unconditional brightness() — a permanent backdrop root for the button's descendants — plus the ':89 compositor-safe' reassurance, adjudicated at GF-DOCK, not asserted proven here.
